summary: After a long run for governor, a family finds its savings spent, its debts heavy and its home as the only cushion left.
realLife: A former lieutenant governor who ran for governor listed his family's debt, mostly a mortgage, and said the family home was effectively their savings. He said the race cost him income because he set aside work that could create conflicts, leaving little income and used-up savings. His wife, who had left an airline job, now worked as an administrative assistant, and he planned to go back to family law and estate work.
gates: The household owns a home with a mortgage.
The candidate ran a long statewide or large race.
The household's savings were drawn down during the race.
weights: Number of children in school or college.
Size of the mortgage against home value.
Whether the candidate gave up outside work during the race.
Whether the spouse has a steady wage.
inGame: Household money, a home and its mortgage, a candidate's filing and campaign money, election results and the spouse's job could carry it; the candidate sidelining paid work needs a job-hours cut during campaign.

turns.what: The household stays comfortable because the candidate kept clients and the spouse's pay covered the house.
turns.pulledBy: Steady outside work, no conflict-of-interest limits.
turns.writesBack: No savings change; no mention in the journal.

turns.what: After the loss the family decides to sell the home and downsize to rebuild savings.
turns.pulledBy: Low savings, no pension, children's tuition due.
turns.writesBack: Household moves; home sold; mortgage ended.

turns.what: The candidate returns to private work within months and the savings recover slowly.
turns.pulledBy: A skilled profession, a ready client list.
turns.writesBack: Candidate job restored; savings rise slowly.
